original_question: Characterize those Scott sober dcpos P for which, for every Scott sober dcpo Q, the product P x Q is again Scott sober.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.8: "Characterize those Scott sober dcpos P for which the products P × Q is Scott sober for every Scott sober dcpo Q."
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's actual target almost verbatim: it asks for a characterization of Scott sober dcpos P such that taking the product with any Scott sober dcpo Q preserves Scott sobriety. It also keeps the scope at dcpos and does not broaden the problem beyond the paper's Section 4 formulation.
missing_details: The paper defines "Scott sober" in Definition 4.4(1): a dcpo P is Scott sober exactly when its Scott space ΣP is sober.
To be fully stand-alone, the acronym "dcpo" should be expanded to "directed complete poset."
The product P × Q should be identified as the product dcpo with the componentwise order.
It should be explicit that the sobriety under discussion for P × Q is the sobriety of its Scott space Σ(P × Q), not the ordinary product topology ΣP × ΣQ.

For paper-faithful context, this question is posed as a refinement of Question 4.6 and is motivated by the preceding observation that if P is a domain, then for any sober dcpo Q, the product P × Q is sober.
refined_question: Let P be a directed complete poset. Characterize those dcpos P for which the Scott space ΣP is sober and such that, for every directed complete poset Q whose Scott space ΣQ is sober, the Scott space Σ(P × Q) of the product dcpo P × Q (with the componentwise order) is sober.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4, Question 4.8, not a broader neighboring problem. The wording of Question 4.8 is essentially the same as your draft. The immediately preceding Definition 4.4 supplies the hidden meaning of "Scott sober," and the surrounding sentences show that the problem is asked as a sharpening of Question 4.6 after noting that domains enjoy this product-preservation property. Although Theorem 5.10 later gives general equivalent characterizations of sobriety for T0 spaces, the paper does not explicitly recast Question 4.8 through those equivalents, so the sharpest faithful rewrite is simply to unpack the Scott-sobriety terminology and specify that sobriety is taken on the Scott space of the order product.
